Write node:test static/structural tests for the browser page of a meeting-room booking app in /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc. Load the Skill `tdd-workflow` if available (else skip). Node 22 built-ins only, no npm install, no HTML parser library: write a small tag tokenizer yourself.

READ FIRST: /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/.team/notes/spec.md section "Page", /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/.team/notes/frontend-page.md, the files under test /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/public/index.html and /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/public/app.js, and the fake-DOM harness /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/helpers/fake-dom.mjs (exports FakeElement, loadPage, listTexts). Do NOT edit public/* or the existing helpers.

Create:
1. /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/helpers/html.mjs — a tiny HTML tokenizer: `parseHtml(text)` → flat list of element nodes {tag (lowercase), attrs: Map (names lowercase; value '' for boolean attrs; supports "..", '..' and unquoted values), start, end (index range of the whole element incl. close tag; void elements end at the start tag), innerText (text with tags stripped and entities < > & " ' decoded, whitespace trimmed), innerHtml, parentTags: [...] (ancestor tags), children}. Skip comments, doctype, and the raw contents of <script> and <style>. Void elements: meta, link, input, br, img, hr. Keep it under 150 lines. Export small query helpers: byId(nodes,id), byTag(nodes,tag), within(outer, inner).
2. /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/page-html.test.mjs
3. /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/page-script-api.test.mjs

Rules: `import { test, describe } from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`. Exact equality for every text/attribute the spec names. Files under 400 lines, functions under 50 lines. No console.log. Run with `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc && node --test test/<file>` until green. If a test fails because the PAGE violates the spec, keep the test and report it.

page-html.test.mjs (read public/index.html from disk):
- `<title>` text exactly 'Room bookings'; exactly one `<h1>`, text exactly 'Room bookings'.
- `<form id="booking-form">` exists, has attribute novalidate. Inside it (descendants): `select#room` with name 'room'; `input#title` type 'text' name 'title'; `input#date` type 'date' name 'date'; `input#start` type 'time' name 'start'; `input#end` type 'time' name 'end'; `button#book` type 'submit' text exactly 'Book'. For each of the five fields exactly one `<label for="<id>">` with exact text (Room, Title, Date, Start, End), and that label does not contain the field (no descendant with that id / no input/select inside the label).
- Outside the form (not a descendant of the form): `input#filter-date` type 'date'; `<label for="filter-date">` text exactly 'Show date' not containing it; `button#show-all` type 'button' text exactly 'Show all'; `ul#booking-list`; `p#error` with attribute role='alert' and empty content (innerHtml.trim() === '').
- Every id appears once.
- No `<option` anywhere (case-insensitive); none of 'Aurora', 'Borealis', 'Cosmos' anywhere in the HTML.
- Exactly one `<script` element; its src is exactly '/app.js'; it has no type, defer, async attribute; its content is empty (no inline script); it is the last element in `<body>`: after its `</script>` only whitespace/comments come before `</body>`, and it is a direct child of body.
- No attribute whose name starts with 'on' on any element (no event-handler attributes). Neither index.html nor app.js contains 'http://' or 'https://' (case-insensitive).
- Also a test that the tokenizer is not fooled: run the same structural assertions helper against a few tiny inline HTML strings that should FAIL (e.g. label wrapping its input, script with defer, script not last, `<h1>` twice, form missing novalidate) and assert the checker reports failure — structure your checks as reusable functions `checkPage(html)` returning a list of problems ([] when fine), test `checkPage(realHtml)` deepEqual [], and each bad variant (made by a small string replace on the real HTML) yields a non-empty list. This proves the checks bite.

page-script-api.test.mjs (read public/app.js):
- Classic script: `new vm.Script(source)` compiles without error; the source has no `import`/`export` statements (regex /^\s*(import|export)\b/m) and no `import(`.
- Deny-list scan of source text (strip comments first; keep string contents): none of window, self., globalThis, location, XMLHttpRequest, innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, createTextNode, querySelector, setTimeout, setInterval, requestAnimationFrame, localStorage, sessionStorage, DOMContentLoaded, 'load', onload, onclick, onsubmit, eval(, new Function, dispatchEvent, setAttribute, classList, appendChild, innerText, location.reload, addEventListener('load'.
- Setup happens at once: after loadPage() (harness) with no await, `calls.length === 2` synchronously (rooms + list requested immediately, no load event awaited).
- Dynamic allow-list check with Proxies: write a local loader (in this test file) like the harness's loadPage, but where `document`, every element from getElementById/createElement, every event object passed to listeners, and every fetch response are wrapped in a recording Proxy. Get trap: record `${kind}.${String(prop)}`, then return `typeof v === 'function' ? v.bind(target) : v` using Reflect.get(target, prop, target); set trap: record and Reflect.set(target, prop, value, target). Unwrap proxies passed into append/replaceChildren is NOT needed if you keep a WeakMap proxy→target and have test-side code read targets only (so test-side inspection is never recorded). For events: build your own event object {type, defaultPrevented:false, preventDefault(){...}} wrapped in a Proxy and call the target's listeners (target.listeners[type]) directly. Fetch: record the options' keys (must be subset of method, headers, body); responses are Proxies over {status, json()}; ignore 'then' on responses (Promise resolution probes it) and Symbol keys used by inspection. Drive a full scenario: rooms reply 200 {rooms:[...3]}, list reply 200 with two bookings, submit the form (set control values first via the targets) with 201 then list reply, submit with 409, click a Cancel → 204 then list, click Cancel → reject, filter change → list 500 {error:'x'}, filter input, show-all click → list 200 {bookings:[]}. Then assert recorded accesses ⊆ allow-list: document.{getElementById, createElement}; element.{textContent, value, type, disabled, append, replaceChildren, addEventListener}; event.{preventDefault}; response.{status, json}. Assert also that the vm context's only browser globals are document and fetch (the harness already does this) and that no ReferenceError/TypeError surfaced (attach process 'unhandledRejection' listener during the test, removed afterwards, and fail if it fires).
- Add one negative self-check: a modified source (string replace in memory, e.g. replace `.textContent = text` with `.innerHTML = text`, or `item.append(` with `item.appendChild(`) run through the same proxy loader records a disallowed member, proving the check bites. Run the modified source from memory in vm, never write files.

Final message: files, number of tests, pass/fail, any spec violation. Keep it short.

content.content: 1 # Spec — meeting-room booking app (owner: supervisor, verbatim user requirements; FINAL, do not ask questions) 2 3 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Node v22. Tests use node:test. Do not use the Fable model. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 ## Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 ## API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. All three files are written and the tests pass: 25 tests, 25 pass, 0 fail (17 in `page-html.test.mjs`, 8 in `page-script-api.test.mjs`). I found no spec violation in `public/index.html` or `public/app.js`.

- **Skill:** `tdd-workflow` isn't in the skill list, so I skipped it.
- **Line counts:** I didn't check them. The tokenizer was written to stay under 150 lines and the test files under 400.
- **Negative self-check:** the spec suggested `item.append(` to `item.appendChild(`. That variant makes `app.js` throw inside `node:test`, which fails the run on an unhandled rejection. I used `option.textContent = room` to `option.innerText = room` instead. Together with the `.textContent = text` to `.innerHTML = text` variant, both are caught as disallowed members.

Files, all in `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/`:
- `helpers/html.mjs`: the tokenizer, with `parseHtml`, `byId`, `byTag` and `within`.
- `page-html.test.mjs`: `checkPage(html)`, which returns `[]` for the real page, and 14 bad variants that each get a non-empty problem list.
- `page-script-api.test.mjs`: the source and deny-list checks, the synchronous two-call setup check, and the full Proxy-recording scenario with the allow-list assertion.

`byId` returns an array of matches, not a single node, so the duplicate-id check can use it.
